data.title: Dubai International Chamber opens representative office in Miami to strengthen trade and investment ties between Dubai and the United States
data.description:
Dubai International Chamber opens representative office in Miami to strengthen trade and investment ties between Dubai and the United States

Dubai International Chamber opens representative office in Miami to strengthen trade and investment ties between Dubai and the United States

PR Newswire

DUBAI, UAE, Nov. 19, 2026

DUBAI, UAE, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Dubai International Chamber, one of the three chambers operating under the umbrella of Dubai Chambers, has opened a new representative office in Miami. The office aims to strengthen business ties between Dubai and the United States and expand trade and investment cooperation between companies in both markets.

The Miami office is Dubai International Chamber's second representative office in the United States, following the opening of its New York office during the Dubai Business Forum – USA, organised by Dubai Chambers in November 2025.

Salem AlShamsi, Executive Vice President of International Relations at Dubai Chambers, stated: "The opening of our new office in Miami marks an important step towards expanding trade and investment partnerships between Dubai and the United States and creating new growth opportunities for the business communities in both markets".

The new office comes amid growing trade between Dubai and the United States. Bilateral non-oil trade reached AED 121.8 billion in 2025, representing an increase of 4.6% compared to the previous year.

The number of active American companies registered with Dubai Chamber of Commerce reached 3,718 by the end of December 2025, recording year-on-year growth of 18.1%. A further 439 American companies joined the chamber during the first nine months of 2026, reflecting continued interest among American businesses in Dubai as a destination for business, expansion, and investment.

The Miami office will strengthen engagement with key public and private sector stakeholders, deepen cooperation with the American business community, and highlight the competitive advantages that make Dubai a leading global business destination. It will also provide information and market intelligence to help American companies enter the Dubai market and expand their operations from the city into international markets.

In addition, the office will support Dubai-based companies seeking to expand into the United States by providing specialised market insights, helping them identify promising trade and investment opportunities, and connecting them with trusted local partners.

About Dubai International Chamber

Dubai International Chamber, one of the three chambers operating under the umbrella of Dubai Chambers, was established to promote Dubai as a global business hub, attract multinational companies and expand the emirate's trade ties with promising markets.

data.title: gategroup delivers specialized inflight catering for Pope Leo XIV's historic journey across South America
data.description:
ZURICH, Switzerland – November 19, 2026 – gategroup, a leading global provider of airline catering and hospitality services, played an integral role in Pope Leo XIV's apostolic journey across South America, providing specialized inflight catering and logistics services in collaboration with airline partners ITA Airways, Aerolíneas Argentinas and LATAM Airlines.

The historic journey began in Rome on November 6, with Pope Leo XIV departing aboard an ITA Airways flight to Montevideo, Uruguay, before continuing to Argentina and Peru. For the inaugural flight, gategourmet Italy provided specialized inflight catering services, bringing together culinary expertise, meticulous preparation and precise coordination at every stage, from menu development and production to final aircraft loading. The menu celebrated the richness and diversity of Italian cuisine, featuring regional specialties ranging from traditional cheeses and Neapolitan pizza to Amalfi lemon desserts.

Bringing regional flavors onboard
In Argentina, gategourmet catered three flight sectors, supporting the operation through coordinated catering production, logistics and aircraft-loading services.

In Peru, gategourmet catered five flights connecting Lima, Chiclayo, Cusco and Pucallpa, before the return flight to Rome, each showcasing the regional cuisine.
Menus developed by LATAM appointed chefs James Berckemeyer and Aldo Yaranga, drew inspiration from the country's Andean and Amazonian culinary traditions, incorporating ingredients such as tricolor quinoa, lúcuma, camu camu and Amazonian cacao.

“Supporting a journey of this significance is both a privilege and an honor,” said Federico Germani, Chief Commercial Officer & President Americas, Asia Pacific, and Middle East at gategroup. “We are deeply grateful to ITA Airways, Aerolíneas Argentinas and LATAM Airlines for the trust they placed in our teams and for the close collaboration throughout this journey. Operations of this nature are only possible through strong partnerships, and we greatly value the opportunity to support this historic visit. We also appreciate the confidence our airline partners continue to place in gategroup and our people.”

Ahead of the long-haul return flight from Lima to Rome, gategourmet's Lima facility prepared an extensive inflight dining program showcasing Peruvian specialties, alongside refreshments and breakfast offerings.

Beyond the kitchen
gategroup’s operation extended well beyond food preparation, necessitating coordination between culinary teams, airline partners and local production facilities across multiple airports.

In Cusco and Pucallpa, gategourmet oversaw catering produced by local culinary partners, coordinated quality verification, and ensured specialized aircraft-loading arrangements and ground-handling services to maintain consistent standards of food safety, quality and service.

The successful execution of this complex, multi-country operation highlights gategroup's ability to combine its international capabilities with local market expertise, delivering tailored hospitality solutions for its airline customers under exceptional operating requirements.

About gategroup
gategroup is a leading global provider of airline catering, retail-on-board, and hospitality products and services. Headquartered in Zurich, Switzerland, the company serves millions of passengers through a network of nearly 300 locations in more than 68 countries. By leveraging innovation and operational expertise, gategroup partners with the world’s leading airlines to create exceptional travel experiences. Learn more at www.gategroup.com

data.title: The Adecco Group global study: AI delivers more value when people are involved in work redesign
data.description:
The Adecco Group global study: AI delivers more value when people are involved in work redesign

The Adecco Group global study: AI delivers more value when people are involved in work redesign

PR Newswire

ZÜRICH, Nov. 19, 2026

New research among 40,500 workers finds well-integrated AI saves more time, while training, worker involvement and human-centered leadership determine whether adoption translates into sustainable performance.

  • AI delivers greater value when it is embedded into how work gets done. Workers using well-integrated AI save 20% more time per day and are more likely to reinvest that time in higher-value work.
  • Worker involvement turns adoption into adaptability. 96% of workers involved in redesigning their work are willing to adapt to changing environments, compared with 29% of those not involved.
  • Work-life balance has overtaken salary as the leading reason people would leave their job. It is now workers' leading reason for considering a move.

ZÜRICH, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Adecco Group (SIX: ADEN) today published the seventh edition of its annual Global Workforce of the Future report, based on a survey of 40,500 workers across 36 countries. The findings show that AI adoption is advancing rapidly, but technology delivers its strongest value when organizations redesign work around people; equip them with relevant skills; and give them a voice in how change is implemented.

AI is now embedded in working life. Nearly three-quarters (74%) of workers use AI agents at work, up from 64% in 2025, and technology occupies four of the five leading influences reshaping work. Yet adoption alone does not guarantee value. The research points to a widening gap between organizations that simply deploy AI and those that orchestrate people, AI agents and workflows as a well-orchestrated hybrid workforce.

Where AI is well integrated into operating workflows, workers report saving 20% more time per day than users experiencing lower integration. They are also more likely to reinvest the time saved in higher-value work and seven times less likely to feel overwhelmed by the need to use AI tools effectively. The findings suggest that productivity gains depend less on access to technology than on how effectively it is embedded into the work itself.

Denis Machuel, CEO of the Adecco Group: "The next phase of AI at work is not about deploying more tools. It is about orchestrating people and technology more effectively. When workers help redesign how work gets done, and receive the training and clarity to adapt, AI creates more value and change becomes easier to navigate. AI delivers its greatest impact when it happens with people and not to people."

data.title: Sophia Space Deploys Orbital Computing Software Across Multiple Kepler Satellites
data.description:
Sophia Space Deploys Orbital Computing Software Across Multiple Kepler Satellites

Sophia Space Deploys Orbital Computing Software Across Multiple Kepler Satellites

PR Newswire

PASADENA, Calif., Nov. 19, 2026

First in-space deployment of Sophia Orbital Operating System (SOOS) aboard multiple Kepler Communications satellites opens the door for organizations to run workloads in orbit and accelerate the future of scalable orbital data centers.

PASADENA, Calif., Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Sophia Space, a pioneer in passively-cooled orbital computing infrastructure, today announced the first in-space deployment of its Sophia Orbital Operating System (SOOS) leveraging the on-orbit compute infrastructure aboard multiple Kepler satellites within Kepler's Tranche 1 optical data relay constellation. The collaboration is advancing the company's effort to deploy scalable computing infrastructure in orbit. This deployment establishes a foundational software layer for Sophia Space's future orbital computing architecture, designed to support computing workloads across individual spacecraft and larger, distributed orbital networks.

 Sophia Space deploys SOOS across multiple Kepler satellites, paving the way for scalable orbital data centers.

Hosted aboard Kepler satellites, the SOOS deployment validates resilient, autonomous software capabilities needed to manage and execute distributed edge computing workloads across multiple spacecraft connected via optical links in the space environment. This software demonstration marks an important step toward dedicated orbital computing infrastructure capable of processing mission-critical data in space, enabling faster insights, greater operational resilience, and more sophisticated space-based data services.

"Building the next generation of space infrastructure isn't about launching an entire data center overnight. It's about proving the architecture, step by step," said Rob DeMillo, CEO and Co-Founder of Sophia Space. "Deploying SOOS in LEO is an important first step. We're beginning with the software foundation, then moving toward dedicated computing hardware, standalone satellites, and ultimately entire constellations. Each mission builds toward a future where computing becomes an integral part of the orbital economy."

The collaboration also highlights the growing convergence of satellite communications and orbital computing, creating opportunities to run AI inference workloads closer to where data is collected and generated. SOOS enables distributed edge computing through managed Kubernetes application deployment and management; software that runs and manages applications across a group of computers. SOOS offers triple redundancy and built-in security capabilities designed to support resilient operations for partners looking to deploy AI inference workloads in orbit across a variety of applications, including missile warning, space domain awareness, maritime awareness, disaster response, atmospheric monitoring and weather intelligence, spacecraft operations, zero-gravity manufacturing, and a host of other potential uses.

"As the space economy grows, communications and computing will become increasingly interconnected," said Caitlin Marsh, president of Kepler US. "Our collaboration with Sophia Space reflects the importance of building an orbital infrastructure ecosystem where data can be processed, managed, and delivered more efficiently. This is an early step toward demonstrating how those capabilities can work together."

SOOS deployment represents the first step in Sophia Space's broader development roadmap, designed to progressively validate the technologies needed to deliver scalable computing infrastructure in orbit. Sophia Space is now open to partner with other companies looking to deploy edge applications in LEO. 

"I want to congratulate the software and operations teams at Sophia Space and Kepler for successfully demonstrating distributed operating system functions across multiple satellites in space and multiple GPUs on each satellite," added Dr. Leon Alkalai, Founder and CTO of Sophia Space. "The Sophia team demonstrated distributed functions essential for satellite system resilience, self-awareness and fault tolerance. These building blocks are essential for any future orbiting data centers infrastructure."

These missions are intended to demonstrate how modular computing infrastructure can scale into distributed orbital networks, while advancing opportunities to work with partners to bring new computing capabilities in orbit.

About Sophia Space

Sophia Space is developing the next generation of orbital computing infrastructure through its modular, passively cooled TILE architecture and Sophia Orbital Operating System (SOOS). Drawing on patented, thermal-management innovations originating at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory and the California Institute of Technology, the company is working to make high-performance computing in space more scalable, efficient, and accessible. Headquartered in Pasadena, California, Sophia Space is building the infrastructure to support a growing space-based economy.

About Kepler Communications

 Kepler Communications Inc. is a space infrastructure provider on a mission to deliver real-time access to space data. With 33 satellites launched to date, Kepler operates the first commercial optical data relay constellation, enabling real-time, continuous space connectivity while supporting advanced on-orbit compute and hosted payload capabilities. Kepler has achieved industry-leading milestones, including the first commercial on-orbit demonstration of SDA-compatible optical inter-satellite links and successful space-to-air and space-to-ground optical communication demonstrations. Headquartered in Toronto, Canada, Kepler is building a global company to enable the future space economy.

data.title: Australian Dollar Slides as Thoughts Turn to RBA Rate Cuts
data.description:
By James Glynn

SYDNEY--The Australian dollar weakened after news the country's unemployment in October surged to its highest level since 2021.

The Aussie fell to around 66.60 U.S. cents after the data was released early Thursday, hitting its weakest levels since January, from around 67.20 U.S. cents just prior.

Economists were surprised by a rise in unemployment to 4.9% in October from 4.7% in September, which brought with it a fall in employment of close to 50,000 jobs over the month.

The data immediately cast doubt on whether the Reserve Bank of Australia would be able to raise interest rates further, after delivering five increases since the start of the year.

To be sure, the discussion in financial markets also turned more fully to the question of when the RBA might start cutting interest rates.

Interest rate swap markets had been pricing a 28% chance of an interest rate rise by February. After the data, that shifted to a 20% chance of an interest rate cut by March.

An interest rate cut by November next year is now fully priced in.

Taylor Nugent, an economist at National Australia Bank, said unemployment is already well above where the RBA had expected it to be in the final months of the year, which supports the case that the interest rate tightening cycle is over.

NAB expects the RBA will start cutting interest rates in August next year as the economy slows and inflation pressures ease.

Currency traders are weighing competing influences as it was only on Tuesday that RBA Governor Michele Bullock reaffirmed her view that inflation risks remain skewed to the upside.

Bullock said the problem with inflation is that it isn't just due to high oil prices, adding that domestic price pressures are also strong, fueled in part by a boom in data center investment.

Also, wages in the third quarter grew at their fastest pace in three years, something that will further stoke fears at the RBA that high inflation expectations are becoming embedded.

Inflation data for October will also be published next week with economists fearing that it could bring more bad news for the RBA.

The central bank recently forecast that inflation won't return to the target of 2.5% until mid-2028, leaving it open to a lot of forecast error.

Still, traders are now more comfortable about ruling out a further interest rate rise by the RBA.

"The weaker-than-expected jobs data reinforces our view, and market expectations, that the RBA's tightening cycle is over and its next move will be a rate cut," said Carol Kong, currency strategist at the Commonwealth Bank of Australia.

CBA is now forecasting two interest rate cuts in August and November, she added.

"The dovish repricing of RBA policy has pushed Australian dollar back to where it started the year. We continue to see the path of least resistance for the currency as lower over the coming months," Kong added.

-- Write to James Glynn at james.glynn@wsj.com

(END) Dow Jones Newswires

data.title: KKR Invests in Gentari’s Renewables Platform in India
data.description:
KKR Invests in Gentari’s Renewables Platform in India

Clean energy solutions company Gentari and leading global investment firm KKR today announced that capital accounts advised by KKR have made a minority investment in Gentari Renewables India Pte Ltd, which holds Gentari’s renewables platform in India. ​​The investment will provide growth capital to support the platform’s continued expansion in the country.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261118076160/en/

India remains a key market for Gentari, underpinned by increasing renewable energy demand, supportive market fundamentals and long-term opportunities. The investment marks an important milestone in the evolution of Gentari’s renewables platform in the country. Today, Gentari's India platform has approximately 8 GW of operating, under-construction and contracted renewable energy capacity, with a robust development pipeline. The platform serves commercial and industrial customers, as well as government entities, through a diversified portfolio spanning solar, wind, hybrid and battery energy storage solutions, helping meet India’s growing clean energy needs. This reflects Gentari’s progress in scaling the business into one of its largest growth platforms. The strategic partnership with KKR brings together Gentari's development, execution and operating capabilities with KKR’s long-term investment and deep infrastructure experience to support the platform’s next phase of growth.

Sushil Purohit, Group Chief Executive Officer, Gentari, commented, "This strategic partnership reflects confidence in the scale and maturity of the platform we have built in India as well as the strength of our growth trajectory. We are pleased to welcome KKR as an investor, given its long-term investment approach and deep experience supporting infrastructure and energy businesses globally. With KKR’s support, we are well-positioned to continue scaling the business as a self-sustaining renewable energy platform focused on long-term value creation."

Hardik Shah, Partner, Asia Pacific Infrastructure, KKR, said, “India’s demand for reliable power is growing rapidly, creating a significant need for continued investment in the country’s energy infrastructure. We believe scaled platforms that can deliver increasingly sophisticated renewable energy solutions will have an important role to play in meeting that demand. Gentari has built strong capabilities across renewable generation, hybrid solutions and energy storage and we look forward to supporting the business in its next phase of growth.”

KKR has been investing in India’s infrastructure sector for more than a decade, with a focus on building and scaling platforms across sectors including renewable energy, power transmission, roads, logistics and transportation. In renewable energy, KKR has invested in Serentica Renewables and Hero Future Energies, building on KKR’s broader approach of supporting and scaling infrastructure platforms in India. Since 2011, KKR’s infrastructure platform has committed more than US$27 billion in energy transition and renewables infrastructure globally.

Following the investment, Gentari will continue to retain strategic oversight and operational control of the platform in India. This milestone reinforces Gentari's long-term commitment to India and supports the next phase of expansion of its renewables platform in the country.

About Gentari

As part of the PETRONAS Group, Gentari is a clean energy solutions company operating across Renewable Energy, Hydrogen and Green Mobility. Through these businesses, Gentari supports customers in addressing evolving energy needs while balancing energy security, reliability, and affordability. With 9.1 GW of renewable energy capacity installed and under construction globally, Gentari has established a growing presence across key markets including Malaysia, India and Australia. Its renewable energy portfolio spans solar, onshore and offshore wind, and battery energy storage, while its hydrogen and green mobility businesses continue to expand. Gentari is also advancing cross-border energy initiatives, including renewable electricity interconnection opportunities in Southeast Asia. By combining expertise across its businesses, Gentari helps customers optimise energy systems, strengthen operational resilience, and create long-term value. Gentari aims to be Asia Pacific's most valued clean energy solutions partner. For additional information, visit www.gentari.com.

About KKR

KKR is a leading global investment firm that offers alternative asset management as well as capital markets and insurance solutions. KKR aims to generate attractive investment returns by following a patient and disciplined investment approach, employing world-class people, and supporting growth in its portfolio companies and communities. KKR sponsors investment funds that invest in private equity, credit and real assets and has strategic partners that manage hedge funds. KKR’s insurance subsidiaries offer retirement, life and reinsurance products under the management of Global Atlantic Financial Group. References to KKR’s investments may include the activities of its sponsored funds and insurance subsidiaries. For additional information about KKR & Co. Inc. (NYSE: KKR), please visit KKR’s website at www.kkr.com. For additional information about Global Atlantic please visit Global Atlantic Financial Group’s website at www.globalatlantic.com.

data.title: EMEA Morning Briefing: Markets Await Anthropic IPO
data.description:
MARKET WRAPS

Watch For:

No major economic events expected; Trading updates for Halma, Sage, Babcock International, JD Sports Fashion, Investec, Johnson Matthey

Opening Call:

European stock futures were mixed, after Asia stocks also painted a mixed picture. The yield on U.S. Treasurys were lower, the dollar strengthened. Gold fell and oil was mixed.

Equities:

European equity futures were mixed ahead of the highly-anticipated initial public offering of Anthropic, which was expected to price its initial public offering after the bell at more than $80 apiece, which would value the AI at roughly $1.5 trillion.

"It's exciting, but...let's remember the statistic that says something like 80% of IPOs over the last 10 years trade below their IPO price in the first 90 days and certainly SpaceX is a good example of that if you want to look at recent history," said Oliver Pursche, senior vice president at financial adviser Wealthspire.

Pursche said the bigger question for Anthropic and the market as a whole is: "Are we going to see any meaningful regulatory changes as a result of the change in Congress?"

Forex:

The U.S. dollar strengthened and rose to new 52-week highs after the minutes of the Federal Reserve's October meeting revealed central bankers' mounting inflation concerns.

FOMC minutes indicated that nearly all members agreed in October that they would have to raise rates in the months ahead, CBA's Joseph Capurso said.

The minutes also showed that two members said an increase of more than 25 bps could be warranted in December, Capurso added

Bonds:

The yield on U.S. Treasurys were lower as risk aversion offset rate-hike anticipation.

Economic data remained weak as the pending home sales index, which tracks home-sales contracts, decreased 4.7% to 63 in October, with activity slowing to levels not seen since the 2008-2010 housing crisis.

Energy:

Oil prices were mixed. U.S. crude oil inventories rose more than expected in a second straight weekly build, according to data released Wednesday by the EIA.

Commercial crude oil stocks excluding the Strategic Petroleum Reserve increased by 3.4 million barrels in the week ended Nov. 13, the data showed.

Crude stockpiles were expected to have risen by 1 million barrels, according to a WSJ survey of analysts.

Metals:

Gold prices were lower but remained at more than one-year lows as markets priced in rate increases from the Fed. The precious metal has been under pressure from a strong dollar and expectations that the Fed will tilt more hawkish to rein in inflation.

Minutes from the Fed's October meeting cemented those views, showing that nearly all members thought tighter policy will ultimately be needed under their most likely scenario for the economy. A few warned that inflation might prove stickier than expected, which could necessitate a shift to a more restrictive stance.

Chart-wise, it's difficult to spot any significant level of support until prices hit $3,500 an ounce, said David Morrison at Trade Nation.

Copper rose, after tumbling to its lowest level in seven months in the previous session.

The metal is one of the beneficiaries of the artificial-intelligence investment boom, ANZ Research analysts said.

The rapid expansion of data centers, along with the generation and grid infrastructure needed to power them, has shifted expectations for copper consumption.

However, a wave of selling hit commodity markets recently, as risk appetite was weighed by concerns that this year's AI-related rally across equity markets has been overdone, they added.

TODAY'S TOP HEADLINES

Wall Street Pledged to Mobilize $500 Billion for Nvidia-But Hasn't Put Up a Dime

Jensen Huang sensed the winds shifting against Nvidia this spring.

In June, Wall Street giants Apollo Global Management and Blackstone announced a megadeal to help Broadcom, one of Nvidia's main rivals, secure $35 billion of chip financing for Anthropic.

Insurgents in Iran's Borderlands Are Becoming a Bigger Challenge for the Regime

Heavily armed insurgents in Iran's restive borderlands are posing a new challenge to the embattled leadership in Tehran, carrying out an increasing number of attacks in recent months that have targeted regime security forces.

Militants armed with rocket-propelled grenades and heavy machine guns have ambushed security patrols and attacked intelligence and police buildings in a province along Iran's southeastern border with Pakistan. Militant groups in that region have conducted more than 70 attacks, conflict data monitor Armed Conflict Location and Event Data found, the highest annual number in at least a decade.

Anthropic Raises $81 Billion in Biggest IPO Ever

Anthropic sold more shares than it planned at a higher price than expected for its initial public offering, setting a record for the largest IPO ever after strong investor demand.

The company behind the Claude chatbot sold 980,000,000 shares at $83 each, which was above the price range it had guided.

KRYS Investors Have Opportunity to Join Krystal Biotech, Inc. Fraud Investigation with SBS Law

Schall, Brown & Schwartz LLP (“SBS”), a national shareholder rights litigation firm, announces that it is investigating claims on behalf of investors of Krystal Biotech, Inc. (“Krystal” or “the Company”) (NASDAQ: KRYS) for violations of the securities laws.

INVESTIGATION DETAILS: The investigation focuses on whether the Company issued false and/or misleading statements and/or failed to disclose information pertinent to investors. Krystal reported its Q3 financial results on November 2, 2026. The Company revealed that data releases related to several of its products would be delayed to 2027 after previously stating that the data would be available in 2026. Based on this news, shares of Krystal fell by nearly 11%.
